name: Герои Эхо недели эльфов — отряд народа белых холмов, отбивший нашествие Иш-Кантуна «Конец Большого счёта» (ADR-0023, ADR-0024; docs/content/герои/состав-героев.md, «Эльфы — Иш-Кантун»; RS.weeks в design/ui/roster.js). Пятеро по герою за цикл II–VI: c2-51 Айтан Сеть из Лиан, c3-51 Нохо Соль Ран, c4-51 Тамай Белый Холм, c5-57 Кельмиль Духовая Трубка, c6-51 Сиуэ Счёт Наоборот. Их осколки видны во вкладке «За души» и в листе отряда недели, а портретов не было — задание 29.09.2026. Рецепт принятых портретов — jobs/heroes-batch-03.json: тот же стиль, запреты и референсы стиля, кадр по пояс, корпус вправо, к врагам, камера чуть снизу; каждый — по способу «Глубокий промт персонажа» (art/style/style.md): кто он и чего хочет сейчас · характер телом · поза словами в миг действия · пять личных деталей из «кто он» и заголовков глав · место. Раса — Забытые: облик ни на кого из нынешних не похож (как Оэлис c1-22), меры Забытых — звёзды, огонь в чаше, глина, свист (лор-аудит, «Голоса народов»). Враги их недели — эльфы Иш-Кантуна: перья, нефритовые маски, обсидиан (jobs/echo-ishkantun.json) — в деталях как трофеи и угроза. Класс — по оружию и действию, школа — по цвету света. Детали, которых нет в «кто он» и главах, — решение агента, по строке в source
style: Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, strong readable silhouettes, deep near-black shadows. Epic, heroic character art: a powerful pose, a low camera, strong light from below. Light tells the story: a few strong sources — crystals and cracks that glow from within — throw colored light upward, the light comes from below. Cold and warm light contrast. Dust motes and grains of sand float in the light. Moderate detail, clean readable forms; the face, the hands and the weapon get the most detail. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime. Match the brushwork, lighting and color handling of the attached style reference images, but do NOT copy their subjects, objects, letters or composition.
negative: No text, no letters, no numbers, no real-world alphabets, no runes or markings that look like writing, no glyphs, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no border or frame around the picture, no gems or badges of rank. No bodies, no skulls, no blood. Only one character in the foreground; a person has exactly two arms and two hands. Not stiff, not passive, not posing like a mannequin; no empty eyes. The hero is not an elf: no long pointed ears.

heroes.frame:
Draw exactly one image in a single pass: no alternative versions, no second attempts, no text in the reply. Format: vertical hero card portrait, 4:5. A close, heroic half-body portrait from the waist or hips up, three-quarter view; no knees, no legs, no feet in the frame. The camera is a little below the hero's chest and looks slightly up, so the hero towers — a legend, not an extra. The hero's body is turned toward the right side of the picture, toward unseen enemies beyond the right edge, and the face is seen in three-quarter view looking to the right. The hero is caught at the peak of an action that shows who they are; the pose carries weight and intent. Head in the upper third, the face large, well lit and readable at small size, with a clear expression; the lower quarter may be darker because the card puts the name there. Rich atmospheric background that tells where the hero lived, with depth and soft focus, darker than the character. Light comes from below and from glowing crystals; rim light separates the figure from the background.

The hero belongs to the people of the white hills — a forgotten people who lived long before all the peoples of today, on the rolling hills of white chalk at the edge of the great dark forest of Ish-Kantun. They look unlike any people living now: tall and lean, with long necks, long narrow faces, high cheekbones and large deep-set eyes; their skin has the warm grey-brown tone of river clay, and they paint lines and handprints of white chalk from their hills on their faces and arms. They wear undyed woven cloth and wraps of pale bark-cloth, necklaces of white shells and chalk beads; their tools are old and simple — wood, bone, white flint, woven vine, fired clay. Their enemies were the long-lived forest elves of Ish-Kantun with feathered cloaks, jade masks and black obsidian blades, who came out of the forest when their Great Count ended; such things appear only as trophies or as the threat beyond the right edge.

jobs.subject: Subject: Aitan Net-of-Vines, a man of the white hills, a trapper who binds enemies, of the Earth school. Who he is: on the forest paths where the feathered archers of Ish-Kantun came down toward the hills, he strung nets of living lianas between the trees, and whole files of archers never reached the hills. Right now an archer has stepped onto his path, and he throws. Character: patient, silent and cunning, a hunter who waits for hours and strikes once. His brows are drawn low, his eyes narrowed and fixed on the prey beyond the right edge, his mouth a thin calm line — no hurry in him at all. Pose, the moment of the throw: the camera is low; he has just hurled a great net of woven green lianas toward the right: it unfurls wide in the air in front of him, its weighted edges of white flint spreading out; his near arm follows through the throw, extended toward the right, the hand still open; his far hand grips the long trailing rope of the net close to his chest, ready to pull it shut. His shoulders twist into the throw, his long body leans forward. Amber-orange light of the Earth school rises from the ground, and small stones and clods jump up around the roots as the net's rope tightens. Details that tell his story: (1) a coil of thick green liana over one shoulder, fresh leaves still on it; (2) his palms and forearms criss-crossed with thin old cuts from the vines, and wound with strips of bark-cloth; (3) at his belt hang several long green and grey feathers torn from the archers his nets have caught; (4) white chalk lines drawn across his cheekbones and down his long neck; (5) a small bone whistle on a cord at his throat, for calling across the hills. Place: a narrow forest path at the edge of the dark jungle of Ish-Kantun at dusk: giant twisted roots and hanging lianas, a glimpse of pale white chalk hills beyond the trees behind him. Warm amber light glows from cracks in the earth of the path below; dust and pollen drift in it.

jobs.subject: Subject: Noho Salt-of-Wounds, a woman of the white hills, a healer of the Water school. Who she is: the healer of the white hills, who closed wounds with salt and chalk; wounds from the black obsidian blades of Ish-Kantun closed under her hands faster than under the hands of their own priests. Right now a fighter of her people has fallen with an obsidian cut, and she will not let him go. Character: stern, fearless and tender at once — a healer who has seen every kind of wound and is not afraid of any; her jaw is set, her large eyes are wide and focused, her lips pressed together in concentration. Pose, the moment of healing: the camera is low; she leans forward toward the right, one knee braced, her whole body reaching toward the wounded beyond the right edge. Her near hand is thrust out toward the right and flings a glittering spray of glowing blue salt-water and white chalk dust that arcs through the air toward the wound; her far hand holds a shallow bowl of white fired clay against her hip, filled with brine that glows sea-blue. Blue light of the Water school swirls around the spray and rises from the bowl. Details that tell her story: (1) on a cord around her neck hang several small black obsidian splinters she has pulled out of wounds — her tally of the lives she saved; (2) her fingers and wrists are white with chalk up to the forearm; (3) a satchel of woven cloth at her hip, spilling coarse white salt; (4) her long dark hair is bound back with a band of pale bark-cloth, a few strands loose from the effort; (5) a white chalk handprint on her shoulder — the mark her people gave healers. Place: the slope of a white chalk hill at night, trampled grass and a few scattered green feathers; the dark forest of Ish-Kantun below with the faint shape of a jade stepped pyramid; blue light glows from wet cracks in the chalk below her and from the bowl.

jobs.subject: Subject: Tamai White-Hill, a man of the white hills, a defender of the Earth school. Who he is: he stood on the top of the white hill where all the paths out of the forest met. The feathered archers of Ish-Kantun changed their ranks three times a day; he was never relieved — not once. Right now it is the third change: a fresh rank of archers draws their bows at him, and he will not step back. Character: immovable, weary to the bone and unbreakable; a heavy calm. His jaw is clenched, sweat and chalk dust run down his temples, his eyes are steady and fixed on the archers beyond the right edge, his brows lowered like a wall. Pose, the moment of the volley: the camera is low; he stands square and huge, turned toward the right, his weight sunk low as arrows strike. His near arm holds up a tall heavy shield of layered hide and whitened wood in front of his chest and face, angled toward the right, and arrows are thudding into it; his far hand grips a heavy wooden club edged with white flint, held low and ready behind the shield. His broad shoulders are hunched behind the shield, his head lowered, peering over its rim. Amber-orange light of the Earth school bursts from the chalk ground where he stands, and chips of white chalk fly up. Details that tell his story: (1) his shield bristles with many arrows fletched with green and grey feathers — a whole day of volleys; (2) a big white chalk handprint painted in the middle of the shield; (3) many feathers from fallen arrows lie in the trampled grass at his feet; (4) old scars across his forearms and a fresh graze on his cheek; (5) a necklace of white shells, several of them cracked. Place: the very top of a white chalk hill at sunset, the grass trampled flat; below him paths wind up out of the dark forest of Ish-Kantun, a jade stepped pyramid rising far away among the trees; the sky behind is deep red and violet — the third change of the day. Warm amber light glows from cracks in the white chalk below.

jobs.subject: Subject: Kelmil Blowpipe, a man of the white hills, a swift hunter of the Air school. Who he is: a hunter of the white hills with a long blowpipe. He struck the jade-masked priests of Ish-Kantun from behind the trees — the very trees they believed were their own. Right now a priest in a jade mask is passing beneath his tree, and the forest is silent. Character: cold, precise and fearless, a ghost of the forest; utterly still before the strike. His large eyes are wide and unblinking, fixed on the target beyond the right edge; his cheeks are filled with breath; his body is coiled and motionless like a drawn string. Pose, the moment of the shot: the camera is low; he leans out from behind the huge trunk of a giant tree, turned toward the right. Both hands hold a long slender blowpipe of dark polished wood to his lips, aimed straight at the right: the near hand steadies it far along its length, the far hand holds it at the mouthpiece; a thin dart has just left the pipe and flies toward the right, trailing a fine spiral of pale white-green wind. Leaves and pollen swirl in the gust (Air). Details that tell his story: (1) at his belt hangs half of a cracked jade mask of a priest, its carved face split in two — a trophy; (2) a slim tube of bamboo with darts tufted with white kapok hangs across his chest; (3) his body is streaked with white chalk and dark mud to vanish among the trunks; (4) a thin band of pale bark-cloth tied around his brow, a single grey feather through it; (5) his bare feet are not seen, but one hand has a missing fingertip, healed long ago. Place: the dark heart of the forest of Ish-Kantun at night: colossal trees with pale bark, hanging lianas, huge leaves; far below, between the trunks, the lit steps of a jade pyramid. Pale white-green light of the Air school rises from glowing moss and small crystals among the roots below.

jobs.subject: Subject: Siue Count-Backward, a woman of the white hills, a battle mage of the Time school. Who she is: she recounted the great stone calendar of Ish-Kantun and found an error in it — one extra day. On that day their Great Count did not begin anew, and the invasion broke. Right now she turns their own count against them. Character: brilliant, cold and fearless; a quiet certainty that terrifies the enemy — she knows something they do not. Her head is held high, her large eyes shine with green light, a faint knowing smile on her lips. Pose, the moment of the spell: the camera is low; she stands tall, turned toward the right, her long neck straight. Her near arm is thrust out toward the right, the palm open, and around her hand and forearm a wide ring of glowing green light made of simple notches and dots spins backward and flies toward the enemy beyond the right edge (Time); her far hand is raised to her chest and holds up, between two fingers, a single small white pebble that glows brighter than anything else — the extra day. Green motes of light stream backward around her like sand falling upward. Details that tell her story: (1) a pouch of dark counting pebbles at her belt, a few spilling out; (2) her fingers are dusted with white chalk from the hills; (3) simple lines of white dots painted along her arms, like a tally; (4) a long cord of knots and small shells wound around her waist; (5) a small bowl of fired clay with a tiny flame hangs from her belt on a thin chain. Place: the foot of a jade stepped pyramid swallowed by the dark forest at night; behind her rises a colossal round stone calendar disc, carved only with concentric rings of plain notches and dots — no glyphs, no writing — and cracked through the middle. Green light of the Time school glows from the crack in the calendar and from the mossy steps below; motes of light drift upward.

Айтан — сеть из лиан летит вправо, моток лианы на плече, перья лучников у пояса, меловые полосы; спокойный, выжидающий. Нохо — брызги светящейся солёной воды и мела вправо, чаша белой глины, отпечаток ладони на плече, чёрные осколки обсидиана на шнуре. Тамай — щит в стрелах с перьями и белой ладонью, дубина, закат третьей смены; внизу кадра модель оставила ровную тёмную полосу — место имени на карточке, в осколке и на плитке не видна. Кельмиль — духовая трубка, дротик в спирали ветра, расколотая нефритовая маска у пояса, бамбуковый пенал. Сиуэ — кольцо зелёного света крутится назад, белый камешек «лишнего дня» у груди, треснувший календарь из колец насечек; внизу — та же тёмная полоса
